name: Step-Up
description: The step-up is a unilateral lower body exercise in which the lifter steps onto a raised platform with one foot and drives through that leg to bring the body fully upright on top of the box. It trains single-leg strength and hip stability and closely mimics functional movements such as stair climbing. Load can be added with dumbbells, a barbell, or a weighted vest.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a box or sturdy bench of appropriate height (typically 30–60 cm). Hold dumbbells at the sides if adding load.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose a box height that challenges but allows the working thigh to be near parallel when the foot is placed on top. A higher box increases glute and hip demand.
steps: Step 1: Place one foot fully on the box — the entire foot, not just the toes.
Step 2: Drive through the heel of the working foot to push the body upright and bring the trailing leg up.
Step 3: Stand tall on top of the box with hips extended and working leg straight.
Step 4: Lower the trailing leg back to the floor in a controlled manner by bending the working knee.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one side before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you step up. Inhale as you lower down.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the trailing leg — the step-up should be powered entirely by the working leg
Only placing toes on the box, reducing stability
Leaning excessively forward on the way up
safety_considerations: Ensure the box or bench is stable and cannot tip
Step fully onto the box before beginning the drive phase
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Fully extend the hip and knee at the top. Control the entire descent.
coaching_cues: Drive through the heel, not the toe
Don't push off the back foot — make the front leg do the work
Stand tall at the top — full hip extension
